M3F Festival 2027: parking, rideshare and getting there

An M3F ride from Scottsdale Sprinters starts with the festival’s own 2027 facts, a rider count and one transportation lead. Festival crews ride a Limo Party Sprinter or the party bus; VIP guests lead with the Maybach Jet Sprinter and the Ultra Luxury Party Sprinter; big groups and company outings take the executive Sprinter, the mini bus, the mini coach or the motorcoach. This guide uses only published facts, leaves the unannounced ones for closer to the date, and turns each festival day into a written pickup, drop-off and ride home.

Last updated: September 24, 2026

Where do you park for M3F 2027?

M3F has no official festival parking for 2027: its FAQ tells guests to use Valley Metro, rideshare, or to park at 4041 N Central Ave, the one address it names; with a chauffeured ride nobody in the group drives, parks or walks back to a car after the last set. The festival’s own FAQ answers the parking question in three lines: there is no official festival parking; use public transport (Valley Metro) or rideshare services; or park at 4041 N Central Ave. It publishes no lot map, no rate, no operator and no capacity for that address, so this guide prints none either. Steele Indian School Park is a busy city park in central Phoenix, and on a festival day the streets around it fill with people arriving from every direction. The festival’s own advice, to come by light rail or rideshare, says as much. Anyone who drives should plan the parking before leaving home, not on arrival. A chauffeured ride takes parking off the list. The chauffeur drops the group near the entrance, where police and event staff allow, and is booked for the ride home. Nobody circles for a space, pays for one, or walks back to it at the end of the night, and nobody has to stay sober to drive.

Where is the M3F rideshare and drop-off area?

M3F has not posted a 2027 rideshare zone: its FAQ tells guests to use rideshare services but names no pickup spot, and no limo or charter drop-off is published for March 5 and 6; a chauffeured ride unloads where police and event staff direct and meets the group at a time set in advance. When the festival posts a rideshare zone, that zone is for rideshare cars. It is not a commercial-vehicle privilege, and a booked Sprinter, party bus or coach follows its own instruction on the day: the directions of Phoenix police and event staff, and the closures in place around the park. The festival does name one entrance: its bike valet is near the entrance at N Central Ave. The chauffeur unloads as close to the entrance as the open streets and traffic staff allow, and the group walks the last stretch. For the ride home, agree on one meeting point before anyone goes in, away from the exit crush. There is no re-entry, so the group leaves once. Outside, the transportation lead confirms where the vehicle is waiting before the group walks toward traffic.

When is M3F 2027, and what time does it start?

M3F 2027 is Friday, March 5 and Saturday, March 6, 2027, at Steele Indian School Park in Phoenix; the gate and set times are not announced yet, and the festival box office opens at 12 p.m. on Friday and 11 a.m. on Saturday, closing at 11 p.m. both days. Every current official source agrees on the dates: the festival’s 2027 lineup poster (Friday 03/05/27 and Saturday 03/06/27), its lineup-by-day, music and passes pages, and the ticket seller the site links. One FAQ line prints the year as 2026, but its question says 2027 and the weekdays are 2027’s: March 5, 2027 is a Friday. Some search results still show an old page title with March 6 and 7; the festival’s current pages all say March 5 and 6. The gate times and set times for 2027 are not published. The only times on the festival’s site are the box office’s: open festival weekend at Steele Indian School Park, from 12 p.m. on Friday and from 11 a.m. on Saturday, closing at 11 p.m. each day. Those are the box office’s hours, not the gates’. The countdown on this page counts to Friday, March 5, Arizona time, and says so. Plan the pickup around the sets you want to see once the festival posts its schedule, then adjust. Your chauffeur works to the time you set, and the reservations team updates the plan when the gate times are announced.

Where is M3F, and which entrance do you use?

M3F is at Steele Indian School Park, 300 E Indian School Rd, Phoenix, AZ 85012, the 72-acre park at Central Avenue and Indian School Road; the festival’s FAQ places its bike valet near the entrance at N Central Ave, and it publishes no other entrance for 2027. The address comes from the festival’s FAQ, and the ticket seller and the City of Phoenix list the same one. The city calls Steele Indian School Park the premiere special event park in central Phoenix. The festival’s FAQ mentions one entrance, on N Central Ave, near the bike valet. A festival map for 2027 is not posted yet; when it is, check which entrance your pass uses. How each pass enters is the festival’s to describe, not ours. Children 12 and under get in free with a ticketed adult, and the ticket seller lists the event as all ages, so a family group can ride together. Tell the reservations team if a child seat is needed.

Can you take the light rail to M3F?

Yes: the festival’s FAQ points guests to Valley Metro, and the B line runs up Central Avenue past the park, stopping at the Indian School/Central Ave station (stop 10006); the festival also offers bike valet near its N Central Ave entrance, so a pair staying near a station can skip the car. The festival’s parking answer names Valley Metro first. Valley Metro’s B line schedule lists the Indian School/Central Ave station, stop number 10006, on its route along Central Avenue. Valley Metro fares apply; its site lists them and the service hours. Transit is a good answer for two or three people who are staying near a station. It is a harder answer for a group of 10 coming from a Scottsdale resort, or for a crew that wants to arrive together and leave together after the last set. That is where a chauffeured ride earns its keep.

Is a chauffeured ride worth it from Scottsdale?

The drive is about 22 minutes from Old Town Scottsdale without event traffic, so the ride is not about distance: it is no festival parking to find, no rideshare wait after the last set, 1 vehicle that keeps the group together, and a set pickup, with nobody in the group driving. From Old Town Scottsdale to Steele Indian School Park is about 22 minutes by Google’s typical time, and about 27 from Kierland. Nobody needs a chauffeur for the miles. The value is what a festival day does to them: no festival lot, streets full of people, and the same crowd leaving together at the end. When the last set ends, the crowd leaves at once, and rideshare prices and waits can climb when that many people request a car together. A booked vehicle turns that into a plan. One cabin carries everyone, so nobody is split across 3 rideshares or left to find their own way. The pickup time and place are set before anyone goes in. Nobody in the group has to drive, so nobody has to stop at one drink or leave early to fetch the car. The honest limit: we cannot drive past closed streets or unload in a travel lane, and we cannot make the exit crowd move faster. The chauffeur is waiting where the open streets and traffic staff allow, and the group walks to it. For two people staying next to a station, the light rail may be the simpler choice.

What is the M3F bag policy?

The M3F bag policy allows clear plastic, vinyl or PVC bags up to 12 by 12 by 8 inches, fanny packs and wallets up to 5 by 7 inches that need not be clear, and empty single-pocket hydration packs; outside food and drink are not allowed, except empty water bottles. Clear backpacks and handbags within 12 by 12 by 8 inches are allowed, as are small clutches, non-professional cameras, phones and GoPros, prescribed medication with a matching ID, sunglasses, hats, earplugs, sunscreen and bug spray. Water stations run throughout the festival, so bring the empty bottle. Not allowed: totems, wagons, folding chairs and large backpacks; professional cameras and audio recording devices; outside food and drink; weapons and drugs; glass containers, lighters, drones and selfie sticks. The festival is fully cashless: every vendor takes credit and debit cards. Anything the gate will not take can stay in the vehicle when it is booked by the hour. With no re-entry, though, it stays there until you leave for the night, so pack for the whole day before you go in.

Is there re-entry at M3F?

No: the M3F FAQ says there is no re-entry allowed, so each guest goes in once and leaves once on each of the 2 festival days; plan the arrival time, what to carry and the pickup before the group reaches the gate, because stepping out to the vehicle ends that guest’s day. No re-entry changes how a day is planned. A group that wants dinner out before the late sets should eat before going in, or plan to leave for the night after dinner. Nobody runs back to the car for a jacket or a charger: what is not in the bag stays outside. It also sets the shape of the booking. A vehicle booked by the hour waits for the whole group at the end; a group that splits, with some leaving early, can book a second pickup for the early leavers or keep one vehicle and one time for everyone. Tell the reservations team which you want.

Which vehicle fits an M3F group?

Festival crews ride a Limo Party Sprinter or the 28-seat party bus; VIP guests lead with the Maybach Jet Sprinter, then the Ultra Luxury Party Sprinter, our pick for M3F, the Maybach Shuttle Sprinter and the Suburban; big groups and company outings take the Executive Black Sprinter, the mini bus, the mini coach or the 56-seat motorcoach. The table uses current published names, seated capacities, hourly rates and minimums, in three groups. Festival crews: the Limo Party Sprinter (12-13 Pax), the Limo Party Sprinter (16 Pax) and the Party Bus (28 Pax). VIP guests: the Maybach Jet Sprinter, the Ultra Luxury Party Sprinter, which seats 15 at $250/hr, the Maybach Shuttle Sprinter and the Luxury SUV (Suburban). Big groups and company outings: the Executive Black Sprinter, the Mini Bus (24 Pax), the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax) and the 56-Passenger Motorcoach. A VIP party larger than the Maybach Jet Sprinter rides in two vehicles, one booking each for the same day and times: the Maybach Jet Sprinter with the Maybach Shuttle Sprinter seats 17, and with the Luxury SUV (Suburban) it seats 15. Count riders for each direction. The group that arrives for the early sets is not always the group that leaves after the last one. Anyone heading elsewhere after the festival comes off the return list before seats are assigned. Each booking covers one festival day. For both days, book each day as its own ride; the same vehicle can be requested for each. For a per-person view: 13 riders sharing the Limo Party Sprinter (12-13 Pax) for 5 billed hours at $175/hr is about $67 each before tax; 15 riders in the Ultra Luxury Party Sprinter for 6 hours is about $100 each. That is arithmetic, not a flat festival fare.

How should the pickup after M3F work?

Use 2 checkpoints after M3F: the group gathers at the meeting point it chose before going in, then the transportation lead confirms where the vehicle is waiting before anyone walks toward traffic, because the 2027 rideshare zone and any charter pickup area are not yet announced. The vehicle waits on an open street, where police and event staff allow. It cannot stop wherever a map pin lands, and guests should not walk into a roadway to reach it. Central Avenue carries both traffic and the light rail, so the exact spot is set on the day. If the group splits inside, pick a landmark to regroup at before the last set, and charge phones before going in. Anyone leaving early or going on elsewhere tells the transportation lead, so the return list stays right. If the night runs long, your chauffeur waits; extra time is billed hourly at the vehicle’s rate, and you can call or text us to extend. For a multi-vehicle group, label each vehicle, its lead and its drop-off. A crew heading to Old Town and a VIP group heading to a resort should not rely on spotting a driver in a crowd.

How far ahead should M3F transportation be booked?

Availability varies by day and by vehicle, so no fixed lead time applies: request a quote with the rider count, the pickup area and which of the 2 festival days you need, and the reservations team confirms what is open across the 11 vehicles listed, updating the plan as the festival announces its 2027 details. The first request needs the day or days, the hotel or home, a likely passenger count, the arrival you want, and the return. A group does not need every name to begin. It does need to say which group is riding: a festival crew, VIP guests or a big group or company outing. During the final 48 hours, confirm addresses, phone numbers and the festival’s newest instructions, including the gate times and any rideshare zone once they are posted. Reach the reservations team at (623) 986-6339 or reservations@scottsdalesprinters.com. A ride booking never includes a festival ticket or pass: those are sold by the festival, final sale.

Frequently asked questions

When is M3F 2027?

Friday, March 5 and Saturday, March 6, 2027, at Steele Indian School Park in Phoenix. The festival’s poster, lineup, passes and ticket pages all give those two days.

What time does M3F start?

The 2027 gate and set times are not announced yet. The festival box office opens at 12 p.m. on Friday and 11 a.m. on Saturday; those are its hours, not the gates’.

What is M3F?

M3F Music Festival is a two-day music and art festival at Steele Indian School Park in central Phoenix, with multiple stages and art installations. It also runs The Community Project, year-round programs for art, music and community.

Where is M3F?

At Steele Indian School Park, 300 E Indian School Rd, Phoenix, AZ 85012. The festival’s bike valet is near its entrance on N Central Ave.

Where do you park for M3F?

M3F has no official festival parking. Its FAQ says to use Valley Metro or rideshare, or to park at 4041 N Central Ave. With a chauffeured ride nobody drives or parks.

Is there a rideshare drop-off at M3F?

The festival tells guests to use rideshare services but has not posted a 2027 pickup zone. A chauffeured ride unloads and picks up where police and event staff allow, at a time set in advance.

Who is playing M3F 2027?

The 2027 lineup is on the festival’s own site, split into Friday and Saturday on its lineup-by-day page. Set times are not announced yet. This guide does not repeat the lineup.

What bags are allowed at M3F?

Clear plastic, vinyl or PVC bags up to 12 by 12 by 8 inches; fanny packs and wallets up to 5 by 7 inches, which need not be clear; and empty single-pocket hydration packs.

Can I leave M3F and come back?

No. The festival’s FAQ says there is no re-entry, so plan to go in once and leave once each day.

Can kids go to M3F?

Yes. Children 12 and under get in free with a ticketed adult, and the ticket seller lists the festival as all ages.

Can we book a ride for both days?

Yes, one booking per day. Each festival day is its own ride, so a Friday-and-Saturday group books two rides, one for each day, and can ask for the same vehicle each time.
